elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 requires Vendor to defend Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates against such claims and resulting damages, losses, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys' fees.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(b), together with the opening defence obligation, covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(b) expressly includes Vendor's breach of Applicable Law within Vendor's indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(c), together with the opening defence obligation, covers unauthorized access to, use of, or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(c) expressly indemnifies for unauthorized access to, use of, or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(d), together with the opening defence obligation, covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(d) expressly includes Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct within Vendor's indemnity.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of the claim to the indemnifying party.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires prompt written notice and provides that delay excuses performance only to the extent of prejudice.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must permit the indemnifying party to control the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 permits the indemnifying Party to control the defence with counsel of its choice, subject to stated settlement protections.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation from the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) covers third-party claims to the extent arising from content or materials Customer provides to Vendor for use in the Services.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(b) covers third-party claims to the extent arising from Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law, without retaining other claim categories.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 contains only the two specified categories and deletes the original indemnity for every claim relating to Customer's use of the Services.

elements.element: Vendor must provide an IP indemnity for third-party claims alleging infringement or misappropriation by the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(a) requires Vendor to defend and indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against third-party IP claims involving the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims caused by unauthorized Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Section 20.4 excludes claims to the extent arising from Customer modifications other than modifications authorized by Vendor.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would not otherwise have arisen.
elements.evidence: Section 20.4 contains this combination exclusion and expressly requires that the claim would not have arisen absent the combination.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims arising from Vendor's compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Section 20.4 excludes claims to the extent arising from Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications.

elements.element: For an actual or likely infringement claim, Vendor must have a remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: Section 20.5 requires Vendor, at its expense, to procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item.

elements.element: For an actual or likely infringement claim, Vendor must have a remedy to modify the affected item so it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: Section 20.5 requires Vendor, at its expense, to modify the affected item into a functionally equivalent non-infringing item.

elements.element: For an actual or likely infringement claim, Vendor must have a remedy to replace the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: Section 20.5 requires Vendor, at its expense, to replace the affected item with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item.

elements.element: If procurement, modification, or replacement is not reasonably available, Vendor must provide a refund remedy for the affected Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 20.5 provides that if the primary remedies are not reasonably available, the affected Services or Deliverables may be terminated and Vendor must refund allocable prepaid Fees and Fees paid for Deliverables Customer can no longer use.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no liability cap or super-cap applicable to Vendor's indemnity, and no language establishing a cap of three times annual fees.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position, including all Vendor indemnity triggers, beneficiaries, procedural requirements, and the narrowed Customer indemnity. It also includes the fallback IP exclusions and remedies, but fails the fallback because no 3× annual-fees super-cap is included. It is not minimal because it adds terms beyond those needed for the complete preferred position, including Vendor Technology coverage, detailed settlement and participation provisions, and fallback exclusions and remedies. The operative language is generally coherent and preserves the requested commercial intent, but the missing fallback cap prevents full fallback compliance.
